summary: Stormproof is a satellite mission design game where the real Sun decides how long your satellite lives. Players design a small Earth-watching satellite to monitor drought in Angola or floods in Jeddah. They choose the camera, solar panels, battery, radio, computer, pointing, fuel, frame, orbit, rocket and launch date, while managing mass, power, budget, data, communications and lifetime. The game then flies the design twice: once through the Sun the forecast promised, and once through the Sun that really happened, using NASA OMNIWeb solar data, NASA DONKI storms and a real orbital-drag model. When a satellite dies early, the report shows exactly why, in days, and suggests the best next fix. Players change one thing and fly again. This matters because launch timing and space weather can cut a mission short: FACSAT-2 was designed for five years, flew into a stronger Sun than forecast, and lasted 926 days. Stormproof turns that lesson into something players feel. It is free in any browser, in English and Arabic, with a Cadet mode for beginners and an Engineer mode with real units.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Stormproof is a browser game where you design a small Earth-observation satellite and the real Sun decides how long it lives. You pick a mission (Angola drought watch, Jeddah flood watch, or one of three challenges), build the satellite from seven part slots and a 1U, 3U or 6U frame, choose the orbit, rocket and launch date, and watch it fly.

HOW IT WORKS

Every design is flown twice: once through the Sun the 2019 forecast promised (the plan) and once through the Sun that really happened (the truth). NASA OMNIWeb daily solar flux and geomagnetic data drive pre-computed NRLMSIS 2.1 air-density tables. A drag equation, da/dt = -(Cd·A/m)·ρ·√(μa), lowers the orbit day by day until reentry, so a stronger Sun means thicker air and an earlier reentry. Real storms from NASA DONKI pause the flight and make the player decide: ride it out or go to safe mode. The report explains the result as a cause chain in days, checks the FCC 5-year and NASA 25-year disposal rules, and suggests the best next fix, found by running small changes through the engine. The player then re-flies and compares the two flights side by side.

VALIDITY

Our model brings FACSAT-2 down on 26 Oct 2025; the real reentry was 27 Oct 2025. Against NASA's launch-year lifetime curves, 18 of 21 points fall within 30%; the 3 misses are disclosed in the README. 164 engine tests pass. Every number in the game is sourced, computed or labelled "game-balanced".

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Most mission games treat satellite lifetime as a fixed number. Stormproof teaches how design, orbit, launch date and space weather are linked by letting players feel it. It is free, needs no login, runs offline, works in English and Arabic, supports solo play or a team of four, and has a Cadet mode for beginners and an Engineer mode with real units. It is for students, university CubeSat clubs and new satellite teams.

CREATIVITY

Plan with the forecast, fly with the truth: the same satellite lives or dies depending on when you launch it.

TOOLS

TypeScript engine with Vitest tests; React 19 and Vite for the web app; Python 3.12, pymsis and NumPy for the data pipeline; Playwright for browser tests; GitHub Pages hosting. No server.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honesty of every number, accessibility for newcomers (after mentor feedback we added Cadet mode), offline use for classrooms, bilingual access, and openly disclosed limits (empirical atmosphere models under-react to storms; one drag fit for FACSAT-2).

Source code: https://github.com/IyadAbouelseoud/stormproof

NASA GIBS imagery (MODIS, HLS, IMERG layers)
